summary: Cross-service idempotency mismatch when retry logic exists in both orchestration layer and SDK (mixed SDK versions)
description:
Issue summary: Customer NoteWave reports repeated downstream tool/function invocations when their orchestration service (service A) calls our API and then fan-outs to two worker microservices (workers B and C). Both the orchestration layer and the workers implement retry logic. The customer is using a mixture of Redwood SDK versions: Python SDK v1.4.2 in the orchestrator and Typescript SDK v1.2.0 in worker B.

Impact: Duplicate side-effects in customer systems (invoice generation, external webhooks) resulting in billing and operational noise. Affects production traffic in us-east, estimated ~0.2% of requests from the customer.

Observed behavior: On transient 502/timeout from Redwood, orchestrator retries the same request (idempotency key set), but worker B (older TS SDK) replays the function/tool call after reconnect and produces a duplicate side-effect. Worker C (Python SDK v1.4.2) correctly de-dupes using confirmation tokens.

Expected behavior: With a client-supplied idempotency key and Redwood SDK semantics, a single logical call should not cause multiple side-effects even when there are retries at multiple layers.

Notes: Customer uses a custom orchestration pattern where the orchestrator forwards the same request payload to workers and attaches a shared idempotency key header named X-Redwood-Idempotency. Workers may also attach internal request IDs. The duplication only occurs for streaming/long-running function calls (>3s generation time).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy a three-tier setup: orchestrator (Python SDK v1.4.2), worker A (TS SDK v1.2.0), worker B (Python SDK v1.4.2).
2) Orchestrator sends a single API request to Redwood with X-Redwood-Idempotency header set to a UUID and instructs streaming function/tool call.
3) Orchestrator fans out to worker A and B; worker A uses TS SDK v1.2.0 and immediately begins a streaming consume of tokens and triggers a side-effect when function return arrives.
4) Simulate a transient 502 from serving runtime (inject via fault-injection in prod staging or throttle the connection).
5) Observe orchestrator retry logic kicking in after client timeout and sending same idempotency key; worker A reconnects and replays the streaming session causing duplicate function execution.
logs: 2026-03-01T14:22:58Z orchestrator INFO outbound request id=9f8b... idempotency=XRD-12345 status=timeout
2026-03-01T14:22:59Z orchestrator INFO retrying request id=9f8b... attempt=2
2026-03-01T14:23:01Z worker-A WARN reconnect detected session=svc-77 cause=stream-disconnect sdk=ts/1.2.0
2026-03-01T14:23:05Z customer reported duplicate webhook deliveries to billing endpoint
investigation: Observed that the TS SDK v1.2.0 lacks the confirmation-token check introduced in sdk v1.3 which prevents replay after streaming reconnects.

API request logs show the same X-Redwood-Idempotency value used across retries, but worker A establishes a new streaming session (different connection id) and SDK v1.2.0 issues the tool call again on reconnect path.

Serving runtime accepted both invocations because the upstream idempotency key is checked at the HTTP request level; streaming session reconnections currently bypass server-side de-dup for in-progress stream-based function execution (design gap).
Hypothesis: combination of (a) client retry at orchestrator level, (b) older SDK reconnect semantics, and (c) server-side per-stream execution isolation leads to duplicate side-effects.
comments: Support (Aisha): Customer reports duplicates only when worker uses TS SDK <=1.2.0. Python SDK v1.4.2 workers do not show duplicates in the same test harness.
SRE (Luis): Reproduced in internal staging with fault injection; created a short runbook to avoid duplicate webhooks while we investigate. See #support/duplicate-fanout thread.
SRE (Luis): Filed INT-842 to track runtime change to enforce idempotency across stream reconnections during in-flight function executions.
Customer (NoteWave engineer): Can we provide a mitigation we can apply today without patching all worker images? Current patch window is 3 weeks.
workaround: Temporary mitigation: Orchestrator should add additional application-level dedupe before issuing side-effects (e.g., store idempotency token in shared DB and workers check prior to executing side-effect). Also suggest adding jittered exponential backoff at orchestrator-level to reduce client-side aggressive retries. Customer can also upgrade TS SDK to v1.3+ to get confirmation-token semantics.
resolution: In progress: short-term mitigation recommended to customer (application-level dedupe + orchestrator backoff). Engineering has opened INT-842 to implement server-side enforcement for stream-reconnect de-duplication and a patch to TS SDK to backport confirmation-token logic. Once INT-842 merges, we'll coordinate a minor SDK release and a patch rollout. Assign follow-up owner in eng: Priya Shah.
next_steps: 1) Engineering to prioritize INT-842 (runtime and API layer change) - owner Priya Shah.
2) SDK team to prepare a TS SDK v1.3.1 backport with confirmation-token behavior and clear upgrade notes - target ETA 2026-03-10.
3) Support to provide the customer a concise runbook for application-level dedupe and sample SQL/Redis checks.
4) After runtime fix, run canary with NoteWave in us-east and monitor duplicates for 48h.
